blogs.title: How DeepSeekMath Turned 7 B Parameters into a Math Powerhouse
blogs.description: A deep‑dive into the data‑centric tricks that let a modest‑size open‑source model rival GPT‑4 on math benchmarks. We’ll explain the FastText‑based web‑crawling pipeline, why Common Crawl math pages beat arXiv papers, and how multilingual data boosted performance on Chinese tests.

blogs.title: From Code to Calculus: Why Pre‑training on Programming Makes Models Better Mathematicians
blogs.description: An accessible walkthrough of the authors’ experiments showing that starting from a code‑focused LLM (DeepSeek‑Coder) gives a measurable lift in both tool‑free and program‑aided reasoning. We'll illustrate the two‑stage vs. single‑stage training setups and discuss the broader hypothesis that coding skills enhance logical reasoning.

blogs.title: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) Explained: Reinforcement Learning for Math Without the Memory Overhead
blogs.description: A friendly guide to the new GRPO algorithm that replaces PPO’s critic with a simple group‑average baseline. We’ll break down the math, compare it to PPO, DPO, and RFT, and show why GRPO can improve accuracy on GSM8K and MATH while using far less GPU memory.

blogs.title: Teaching LLMs to Reason Step‑by‑Step: Chain‑of‑Thought, Program‑of‑Thought, and Tool‑Integrated Prompts
blogs.description: An overview of the three instruction‑tuning formats used in DeepSeekMath—CoT, PoT, and ToRA—and how each helps the model solve problems with or without Python tools. Includes concrete prompt examples and a discussion of when one style outperforms the others on benchmark datasets.

blogs.title: What Makes a Math Benchmark Hard? Inside the MATH Competition Dataset and DeepSeekMath’s 60% Self‑Consistency Leap
blogs.description: A layperson’s look at the MATH benchmark’s difficulty level, why achieving >50% is considered breakthrough for open models, and how self‑consistency sampling (64 samples per question) pushes DeepSeekMath’s score from 51.7% to 60.9%. We’ll also compare open vs. closed models and what remains challenging.
